text.p: - Russian passenger airplane builders accuse state-owned carrier Aeroflot of undermining their business by turning to American-manufactured jets.
- The Russian government is due to nationalise Agroprombank shortly, others may be in the wings.

- Deputies of the Council of Europe deputies say they want to invite Chechen rebel commander Aslan Maskhadov and Russian security chief Alexander Lebed to Strasbourg to promote a stable and fair peace in the separatist republic.
- The state is tightening its grip on all major oil-producing companies.
- The Russian Central Bank says individual commercial banks may be in trouble but no systemic crisis is looming.
- Drafts of new low-denomination Russian banknotes due to be presented to the public in October prompt rumours that Russia will knock zeros off the rouble in some form of monetary reform.
- Foreign passenger jet producers take on their Russian competitors for a bigger share of the domestic market where Russian makers seem to be loosing ground to the opposition.
- Over 200 unique antique manuscripts seem to have vanished from Russia's State Library, the biggest in the country. The disappearance was discovered in a routine check.
